source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: For V1, what simple, reliable implementation approach would you use for the spout? It must provide a smooth, controlled pour while remaining easy to clean between uses. A proper seal should prevent liquid from leaking into the base, and the open/close mechanism needs to operate cleanly without dripping.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Key Design Details

1\. Valve / flow control — I need a simple open/close valve or tap that prevents constant dripping and uncontrolled pouring.

2\. Seal at the bottom — This is critical: the bottom bowl seal must prevent external leaks as well as seepage into the electronics.

3\. Cleaning — Because matcha + milk leaves residue, the spout should either be removable or easy to flush and clean.

4\. Flow rate — I need a smooth, controlled stream rather than a slow drip or an explosive pour.

value_updates.flow_rate_extremes: neither a slow drip nor an explosive pour

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Could the spout be revised to match the diagram more closely? I’m unsure whether Matcha will retain the same consistency after running through the proposed spout, and it will not preserve the frothiness.

value_updates.beverage_preservation: retain matcha consistency and frothiness during dispensing

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Although this is a significant change to the engineering scope, I can make it work. I haven’t been able to find an off-the-shelf spout that closely matches the appearance of the one in your renders, but I did find an option that should function well. A solenoid valve would sit directly beneath the bowl, preventing any matcha from entering the spout until the button is pressed; releasing the button would stop the pour. Since no matcha would remain in either the spout or the tubing, its frothiness will be maintained. Please review this option: <https://www.amazon.com/Stainless-Pourers-BALTRE-Vinegar-Suitable> Alternatively, if keeping the appearance of the original rendered spout is more important, I could fabricate a custom version, though it would not be made from steel.

value_updates.dispensing_path: gravity-fed through a solenoid valve directly beneath the bowl, with matcha entering the spout only during dispensing

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Nolan — overall, the BOM is exactly the direction I was hoping for, and I really like it. Before we finalize anything, though, I’d like your input on a few details:

• Motors — could 450 RPM be too low for producing a strong, frothy matcha texture? Would increasing the speed make sense if we can still retain enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality, would a stainless-steel or milk-frother-style head perform better than the resin whisk?

• Spout — I want to keep the solenoid approach. For both texture and the overall visual experience, the pour needs to remain clean, controlled, and seamless: mix → open → pour.

• Splash / mess control — events make this especially important. The design should provide:
– minimal to no splashing during mixing
– a smooth, controlled spout flow without sputtering
– no dripping while the valve is closed
– effective sealing so liquid cannot leak into the base
– a splash guard or lip around the bowl if needed

• Cleaning — if possible, the bowls and spout components should either be removable or easy to clean.

Everything else looks great. What are your thoughts on these points, and would you adjust anything before we finalize the BOM?

value_updates.pour_sequence: clean, controlled, and seamless mix → open → pour
